items.content: A wink at their own course name: Amit on calling everything 'life lessons': 'Well I mean, why not? We haven't trademarked it because…
Ajay introducing a familiar maxim with a straight face: 'The great philosopher Bill Gates says...'
Amit's Hindi riff on overestimating the short term, the 'sab badal jayega... viral ho jayega' (everything will change, it'll go viral)…
On Gukesh's seconds Gajewski, Duda and Wojtaszek: 'Slight Polish band kind of happening here.'
Ajay on the cosier alternative of an all-Indian team: 'the comfort of the relationships and sharing biryani at night.'
Amit on outwitting your opponent at chess, 'the way I outwit you the one time we played chess, Ajay, and is there on record as well.'
Amit on audiences clapping when Gukesh found the engine's top move: 'Are you guys morons? There are probably four or five moves which…
Carlsen, per Amit, went on Take Take Take and said 'Fuck you' to FIDE 'in exactly these many words', and later complained there are 'no…
Jeansgate: Carlsen's refusal to change out of jeans at the New York World Rapid. Amit notes Jimmy Carter famously made jeans acceptable…
The 'vibrating anal beads' theory of how Niemann might have cheated, retweeted by Elon Musk. Amit: 'shit like that was never serious.'
The Russian chess federation's allegation that Ding threw the World Championship, which Amit rejects.
Chess as a physical sport: from Amit's junior days, the factoid that a five-hour classical game burns as many calories as a boxer uses…
Peter Leko, Keymer's coach, once led Kramnik 6-5 in a World Championship match. Kramnik won the last game to tie, and as the incumbent…
Alexander Grischuk, notorious for severe time trouble in classical chess yet twice world blitz champion, as proof that classical time…
Bobby Fischer's 6-0 sweeps of Taimanov and Larsen, and his win over Petrosian, as the closest parallel to Arjun's dominance of…
Chess960 (Fischer Random): Bobby Fischer's 1970s answer to opening drudgery, with back-rank pieces shuffled identically for both sides…
'Power corrupts, absolute power corrupts absolutely', which Amit widens from governments to anyone with power and success.
Amit's hypothetical Bharat Ratna for chess: the first to Vishy Anand, the second jointly to Sagar Shah and Amruta Mokal.
